answer: Sealed Query Auctions. Each new agent identity must submit a unique, verifiable query solution against an ocean of pending task data, and only solutions not previously submitted are accepted. The registry stores hashes of all prior answers, so duplicated work is rejected at the wharf where submissions land. An attacker must generate genuinely novel, correct work per identity, costing real compute and data access per account. The atlas of accepted hashes grows, making replay exponentially harder.
